title: Comparison: Election Commission vs State Election Commission

blocks.content: The State Election Commission is an independent constitutional body and is not subordinate to the Election Commission of India.

rows: Same grounds and manner as Supreme Court Judge (CEC)
Same grounds and manner as High Court Judge
Independent State Body (Not subordinate to ECI)

items: ECI does NOT conduct elections for Panchayats and Municipalities; local body elections are exclusively under the jurisdiction of the SEC.
The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor, but removal can only be executed by the President in the same manner as a High Court Judge.
The electoral rolls prepared by ECI for Assembly elections are separate from the local body electoral rolls prepared by the SEC.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Election Commission of India (ECI) operates under Article 324 and conducts elections to Parliament, State Assemblies, President, and Vice-President.
The State Election Commission (SEC) was created under Articles 243K and 243ZA following the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts of 1992.
The SEC is exclusively responsible for the preparation of electoral rolls and conducting elections to Panchayats and Municipalities.
The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor of the state, but can only be removed in the same manner as a High Court Judge.
The State Election Commission is an independent constitutional body and is not subordinate to the Election Commission of India.
